newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Food experts back labels on gene soya and maize.
newsitem.headline: Food experts back labels on gene soya and maize.

text.p: European Union food experts supported a proposal to label genetically modified products already cleared for sale but delayed a decision until June, a Commission spokesman said on Thursday.
Gene-modified soybeans developed by Monsanto and a maize strain developed by Ciba Geigy, which were approved by the EU last year, would be affected.

The spokesman, Jochen Kubosch, said that the EU's Standing Committee on Foodstuffs, composed of experts from the 15 member states, backed the proposal to extend labelling rules for novel foods coming into force on May 15.

"There was a positive opinion. A vote will be taken at the next meeting in early June," he told a news briefing, adding that the committee clarify the scope of Regulation 258/97 on novel foods and novel food ingredients adopted on January 27.

The proposal stated that novel food labelling rules to protect consumer health and ensure fair competition in the EU market, should automatically apply to Monsanto's gene-modified soybeans and Ciba Geigy's maize strain because they are no longer "equivalent" to an existing food or food ingredient.
The foodstuffs panel is one of eight scientific committees advising Emma Bonino, who was appointed food safety commissioner early this year following the public health scare over mad cow disease.
